title: Console fidelity gating + trace-sample strategy + cost-heatmap MVP cut
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Reduce initial surface area for console observability while preserving high-value signals for platform customers. This ticket defines the scoped MVP cuts and gated fidelity model for dashboard tiles, trace sampling, and the new cost-heatmap preview. The goal is to ship a safe, low-cost observability release that: (a) surfaces latency and error hotspots at route level, (b) provides a lightweight trace sampling heuristic for tail latency investigation, and (c) exposes a cost delta heatmap card that estimates token cost by route for the last 24h.

Scope decisions: 1) Dashboard tiles: include aggregated Route Latency, Route Error Rate, 24h Request Volume, and Cost Delta Heatmap (estimated). Exclude: full per-token breakdown, per-token timeline graphs, and long-retention histograms for MVP. 2) Tracing: implement probabilistic trace sampling with weighted sampling for high-latency requests (sample >= 1% by default, up to 10% for p95+ anomalies). Exclude: full distributed-trace waterfall UX, flamegraph view, and advanced trace correlation for MVP. 3) Cost Heatmap: show per-route estimated token spend buckets (Low/Medium/High) and day-over-day delta. Exclude: per-user cost attribution and hourly bucketed chargeback for MVP.

Rationale and trade-offs: shipping trimmed tiles saves aggregation compute and storage costs, lowers telemetry budget, and reduces rollout risk. The trace sampling heuristic balances signal for debugging vs ingestion cost; it intentionally biases sampling toward slow requests to enable triage. The cost-heatmap is intentionally approximate (using cached per-route token-rate extrapolations) to avoid expensive per-request charge accounting in the initial release.

Associated artifacts: PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PRD-console-observability-2025, design mocks: https://drive.redwood.com/console/heatmap-mock-v2.png, spec doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/console-fidelity-gating.md, measurement dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/console-telemetry-mvp
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard contains aggregated Route Latency, Route Error Rate, 24h Request Volume, and a Cost Delta Heatmap card visible to users in the beta orgs
Trace sampling implemented server-side with configurable base rate (1%) and escalator rule: sample up to 10% for requests measured above p95 latency threshold
Cost Heatmap shows per-route buckets with day-over-day delta and links to route detail drilldown (route detail shows sample count and estimated spend)
Server telemetry budget remains under the project cap (target: <= 40% of telemetry budget for first 30 days), validated by e2e tests and loadbench
Design review approved and accessibility basic checks passed (keyboard nav, color contrast for heatmap buckets)

Fallback behavior defined: when telemetry budget exceeded, console falls back to 'summary-only' mode (Route Latency + Error Rate) and hides heavy heatmap card, with visible banner explaining degraded mode
End-to-end tests and a canary rollout plan exist with feature-flag gating and telemetry alerts on error/latency/regression thresholds
